claims.text: Oxidation resistance and material integrity in high-temperature MPEAs are governed by formation of a continuous, adherent oxide layer enriched in high oxygen-affinity elements.
Al and Cr are high oxygen-affinity elements relevant to protective oxide formation in MPEAs.
Increasing the concentration of high oxygen-affinity elements preferentially promotes development of a continuous, adherent oxide layer.
Higher Al and Cr concentrations promote preferential formation of a stable, protective oxide scale.
A stable protective oxide scale limits oxygen ingress into the underlying alloy.
Limiting oxygen ingress slows oxidation kinetics.
The protective oxide barrier helps preserve the underlying alloy's microstructural integrity.
MPEAs with elevated high oxygen-affinity element levels will have lower oxidation rates and lower mass gain than comparable alloys with lower levels.
MPEAs with elevated high oxygen-affinity element levels will show less scale spallation and degradation than comparable alloys with lower levels.
An otherwise similar MPEA with minimal enrichment in high oxygen-affinity elements will develop a less protective, discontinuous oxide layer.
A less protective, discontinuous oxide layer results in higher oxidation rates and accelerated material degradation.
The proposed governing behavior applies to MPEAs in air or similarly oxygen-rich atmospheres at temperatures up to approximately 1200°C.
Significantly different oxygen partial pressures may limit the applicability of the proposed mechanism.
Alloy phase instabilities unrelated to oxide formation may limit the applicability of the proposed mechanism.
The critical concentration needed for protective oxide formation varies with alloy system and test conditions.
